actions.action: Pull out the Mother of Thousands (Kalanchoe) plantlets, roots included
Recheck in a few weeks for resprouting Kalanchoe bits
Scrape off the top 1-2 inches of soil and replace it with fresh mix
Check whether the roots are circling, poking out of the drainage holes, or root-bound, and whether the soil stays soggy
If needed, repot into regular potting soil with about 30% perlite
Move the plant to full sun or at least 6 hours of bright light
Water when the top 1-2 inches of soil are dry
Fertilize with a balanced fertilizer at half strength every few weeks in the growing season
Prune the leggy stems back by about a third
Deadhead the seed pods if you don't want self-seeding
If the leaves keep yellowing, check the roots for rot

reason: The answer lists low nutrients from the lean mix and Kalanchoe competition only as possibilities, while emphasizing low light, and it discourages a full repot into less draining soil, the fix that worked, offering it only as a conditional step alongside fertilizing and weeding; nothing it recommends is likely to harm the plant.
